title: Vinegar Acidity Analysis (Neutralization)
learning_goals: Determine acetic acid molarity through sodium hydroxide titration
Identify stoichiometric neutralization equivalence point with phenolphthalein

rules.text: Protective safety goggles must be equipped before handling active chemicals.
rules.hint: Put on safety goggles from the equipment tray before opening reagent bottles.

rules.text: Chemical-resistant gloves must be worn before manipulating hazardous reagents.
rules.hint: Equip protective nitrile gloves to prevent direct skin contact with corrosive reagents.

rules.text: Buttoned laboratory coat required before beginning experiments in active lab zones.
rules.hint: Fasten your laboratory coat to protect clothing and skin from chemical splashes.

rules.text: Analytical digital balance must be tared to zero with container in place prior to weighing samples.
rules.hint: Place container on balance pan and press Tare to reset display to 0.000 g.

rules.text: All beakers, vials, and solutions must be explicitly labeled with contents and concentration.
rules.hint: Apply label specifying reagent identity and molar concentration to every container.

rules.text: Always add acid to water slowly; never pour water directly into concentrated reagents.
rules.hint: Pour acid slowly down the side of the container into water with constant stirring.

rules.text: Rinse burette with titrant and never exceed graduated volumetric capacity.
rules.hint: Flush burette walls with titrant to condition it and never fill beyond the 50 mL graduated zero line.

rules.text: Administered medication dose must not exceed safe therapeutic threshold.
rules.hint: Verify dosage calculation against patient body weight and maximum therapeutic boundaries.

rules.text: Chemical, biological, and sharps waste must be disposed into designated segregated waste receptacles.
rules.hint: Discard spent chemical reagents into the designated chemical waste carboy.

rules.text: Decontaminate hands and remove PPE in proper aseptic sequence before exiting laboratory.
rules.hint: Remove gloves and coat without touching exterior surfaces, then wash hands with soap for 20 seconds.

wear_ppe: Put on all required safety gear: goggles, gloves, and lab coat.
rinse_burette: Condition the burette by rinsing with a small portion (5 mL) of NaOH titrant.
fill_burette: Fill the burette with 0.1 M NaOH up to 50 mL.
pipette_analyte: Pipette 25 mL of vinegar analyte into the conical flask.
add_indicator: Add 2-3 drops of phenolphthalein indicator to the flask.
titrate: Carefully dispense NaOH titrant into the flask.
swirl: Swirl the conical flask to ensure complete chemical mixing.
record_endpoint: Observe persistent pale pink color change and record final endpoint volume.
dispose_waste: Dispose of chemical contents into designated chemical waste bin.
wash_hands: Remove PPE and wash hands thoroughly at the sink.
submit_report: Submit the completed acid-base titration laboratory report.

common_mistakes.remedy: Always add 2-3 drops of indicator before dispensing titrant to observe equivalence color transition.
Add titrant drop-by-drop near expected stoichiometric equivalence volume.
